definitions.explanation: The quality or degree of being sweet. Used especially when discussing food and drink.

examples.japanese: このりんごは{甘|あま}みが{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: This apple has a strong sweetness.

examples.japanese: {砂糖|さとう}を{加|くわ}えて{甘|あま}みを{出|だ}す。
examples.english: Add sugar to bring out the sweetness.

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}を{煮込|にこ}むと{自然|しぜん}な{甘|あま}みが{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: When you simmer vegetables, a natural sweetness comes out.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{甘|あま}い (sweet) → {甘|あま}み (sweetness). The suffix み converts adjectives into nouns indicating the quality or degree.

KANJI NOTE:
Also written as {甘味|あまみ}. Note that {甘味|かんみ} (read かんみ) means "sweets" or "dessert" — a different word.

SIMILAR PATTERN:
- {甘|あま}み (sweetness), {辛|から}み (spiciness), {苦|にが}み (bitterness), {酸|す}み (sourness)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘|あま}みがある: to have sweetness
- {甘|あま}みが{強|つよ}い: strongly sweet
- {自然|しぜん}な{甘|あま}み: natural sweetness
- {甘|あま}みを{引|ひ}き{出|だ}す: to bring out the sweetness
